records.title: Zanfretta — the Torriglia night patrol
records.place: Marzano di Torriglia, Genoa, Italy
records.explanation: Sceptics say the grass imprint matched the place where the owners tied a horse, that regression hypnosis can create false memories, that the beings resembled characters in popular 1978 Italian TV and comics, and that the “footprints” were puddles. Italy’s national UFO centre (CUN) judged the case unreliable.
records.shape: Red oval craft over 10 m across; later a triangular craft
records.witnesses: Pier Fortunato Zanfretta (a security guard); 52 other statements
records.summary: At about 11:30 p.m. on December 6, 1978 the 26-year-old security guard Pier Fortunato Zanfretta, on patrol at Marzano, in the municipality of Torriglia, noticed four lights in the garden of a mansion called Casa Nostra and then a red oval object more than ten metres across. He radioed his supervisor that “they are not men”, then contact was lost; he was found unconscious and in shock. He described three-metre beings with mottled skin, yellow triangular eyes and clawed feet. A semicircular imprint of flattened grass was found in the garden, and Carabinieri Brigadier Antonio Nucchi collected 52 statements from people who had seen strange lights that night. A neurologist found no mental disturbance in January 1979. Zanfretta later described further abductions, eleven in all between 1978 and 1981, which are the most disputed part of the story.

He radios that “they are not men”; contact is lost.

records.summary: Returning from a photo-reconnaissance sortie in a G.91R, Italian Air Force pilot Giancarlo Cecconi was asked to identify an object tracked by Istrana radar over Treviso air base. He found a dull black, capsule-shaped object about 6–8 m long at about 1,300 m. He made passes within about 100 m and took more than 80 photographs with the aircraft's reconnaissance cameras. Then radar and the tower both lost it.

records.title: Pranles — the yellow light with a turning blue beam
records.place: Pranles, near Les Ollières-sur-Eyrieux, Ardèche
records.shape: A stationary yellow-orange light projecting a blue beam that turned through 360°
records.witnesses: Two couples in neighbouring houses; the first witness a scientist who worked on light and colour
records.summary: From 22:45 to 23:28 on July 21, 1979, a couple at Pranles, in the Ardèche, watched a stationary yellow-orange light on top of a ridge towards the Serre de Pieroulet, like a lighthouse, projecting a blue beam that turned steadily through 360° and swept the ground. No sound was heard. As the husband, a scientist who worked on light and colour, prepared to take a photograph, it went out. Their neighbours had seen the same light in the same direction before closing their shutters at about 23:00. He reported it to the gendarmerie the next day. Re-examining the case decades later, GEIPAN found that a helicopter with a searchlight was the only plausible explanation, but a blue beam from a yellow source, turning continuously for no purpose, did not fit it. The case stays class D, unexplained, though GEIPAN notes it is near the line between unexplained and unusable because no field investigation was made at the time.

records.title: Val Johnson — deputy's patrol car struck by a light
records.place: Near Stephen, Marshall County, Minnesota
records.explanation: UFO researchers (Allan Hendry, Jerome Clark) consider it significant. Skeptic Philip Klass argued it was a hoax and that Johnson damaged the car himself. The patrol car is on display at the Marshall County museum.
records.shape: Beam of bright light just above the road

Both his watch and the car's clock were 14 minutes slow. A doctor compared his eye irritation to "welder's burns".

records.summary: Forestry worker Robert Taylor walked into a clearing on Dechmont Law and saw a large dome-shaped object hovering. records.title: Cergy-Pontoise “abduction” (hoax)
records.place: Cergy-Pontoise, Val-d’Oise, France
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: A hoax. GEIPAN, which reviewed the police and gendarmerie inquiry and its own analyses, calls it “a hoax whose course discredits the scientific work”; one of the friends is reported to have admitted years later that he made the story up.
records.shape: A light over the road that wrapped the car in fog and small flashing spheres
records.witnesses: Three young men; the police and gendarmes arrived after the call
records.summary: Before dawn on November 26, 1979, a young man telephoned the police at Cergy-Pontoise to say his friend had been “abducted by a UFO”. Three friends said they had been loading jeans to sell at a market when a light appeared over the road; the driver went towards it, it wrapped the car in fog and small flashing spheres, and when the fog cleared he was gone. Seven police officers and gendarmes searched; the story became national news. The missing man reappeared at a friend’s flat on December 3, with a journalist present, saying he had woken in a cabbage field. GEPAN’s technical note found that the witnesses’ accounts diverged from the start, that a blood test gave no sign of time in weightlessness, and that cabbages said to have been dried by the light had been left to rot as fertiliser by their owner. GEIPAN classes the affair as a hoax.

records.title: La Joya air base pursuit
records.place: La Joya air base, Arequipa, Peru
records.explanation: Peru’s air force kept the case quiet for decades; no explanation has been published. Peru has since set up an office (now DIFAA) for aerial anomalies, and U.S. documents on the case were later released.
records.shape: Large balloon-shaped object
records.witnesses: Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas; some 1,800 people at the base
records.summary: On the morning of April 11, 1980 about 1,800 people at the La Joya base saw a large, balloon-shaped object hanging still at around 500 metres. Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas, 23, took off in a Sukhoi Su-22 and fired 64 rounds at it without effect. He reported that it climbed away at up to 950 km/h, reaching about 19,200 metres, and stopped so suddenly that he had to swerve to avoid it. Peruvian army radar was said to show only his aircraft, while operators saw the object by eye. The engagement is said to have lasted 22 minutes, until his fuel ran low. The Peruvian Air Force kept the matter classified for decades; U.S. defence documents titled “UFO sighted in Peru” have since been released.

records.title: Paul Bennewitz and the lights over Manzano
records.place: Kirtland Air Force Base and the Manzano weapons storage area, Albuquerque, New Mexico
records.explanation: Nothing Bennewitz filmed or recorded was ever shown to be a craft. What is documented is what happened next: once he took his films and recordings to Kirtland, Air Force counter-intelligence and the ufologist Bill Moore, by Moore’s own account in 1989, fed him forged papers and stories of alien bases, apparently to steer him away from classified work near the base. The airman Richard Doty later said he had been tasked with exactly that. The “Dulce base” legend grew out of it.
records.shape: Lights moving over the Manzano storage area at night
records.witnesses: Paul Bennewitz, physicist and owner of Thunder Scientific; officers of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations at Kirtland
records.summary: Paul Bennewitz ran Thunder Scientific, an instrument firm next to Kirtland AFB, and his house in Four Hills overlooked the Manzano weapons storage area. From July 1979 he filmed lights over Manzano and recorded what he took for coded radio signals, and came to believe they were alien craft linked to the cattle mutilations then in the news. In 1980 he took a woman’s abduction story, recovered under hypnosis, as evidence of an underground base, and on October 24 he contacted Kirtland; on November 10 he briefed officers there. Instead of dismissing him, investigators and Moore fed him forged documents and tales of alien bases near Dulce. Bennewitz wrote to Senator Pete Domenici in 1981 and in 1988 drafted “Project Beta”, a plan to attack the base; that year he barricaded himself at home and spent a month in a psychiatric unit. Greg Bishop’s Project Beta (2005) and Mark Pilkington’s Mirage Men (2010) tell the story.

timeline.text: Bennewitz starts filming lights over Manzano and recording signals.
A woman’s hypnosis sessions in his garage give him the “underground base”.
He contacts Kirtland AFB.
He briefs officers at the base.
He writes to Senator Domenici about bases near Dulce.
He writes “Project Beta” and is hospitalised.
Bill Moore says he helped feed Bennewitz false information.

records.title: Rendlesham Forest
records.place: Rendlesham Forest, outside RAF Woodbridge, Suffolk
records.explanation: The Ministry of Defence found no threat and did not investigate further. Skeptics attribute the lights to a fireball, the Orford Ness lighthouse (visible through the trees in the same direction) and bright stars.
records.shape: Metallic lit object in the forest; star-like lights
records.witnesses: USAF security police; Lt. Col. Charles Halt
records.summary: USAF security patrols at the east gate of RAF Woodbridge saw lights descend into the forest and went in to investigate. Two nights later deputy base commander Lt. Col. Charles Halt led a team that took radiation readings at three ground depressions and recorded his observations on a micro-cassette. His memo to the MoD is one of the most famous UFO documents in Britain.

timeline.text: Patrol sees lights descend into the forest.
Three depressions and marks on trees found; police called.
Halt’s team takes radiation readings; flashing red light to the east.
Halt memo sent to the Ministry of Defence.

points.note: Lights appear to descend near the east gate
Moves off toward the farm and field

sources.label: The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files

records.title: Cash–Landrum incident
records.place: FM 1485 near Huffman, Texas
records.explanation: Army and Air Force inquiries found no helicopters or craft that matched; the witnesses’ lawsuit against the U.S. government was dismissed in 1986. Skeptics question the medical and helicopter claims.
records.shape: Diamond-shaped object venting flame; escorted by ~23 helicopters
records.witnesses: Betty Cash, Vickie & Colby Landrum; other motorists
records.summary: Driving home through the pine woods north-east of Houston, Betty Cash and Vickie Landrum with her grandson said a blazing diamond-shaped object hovered over the road, radiating heat. As it rose, they counted about two dozen helicopters, many resembling CH-47 Chinooks. All three reported injuries afterwards, and they sued the U.S. government.

timeline.text: Light above the trees; object then hovers over the road ahead.
Object rises; helicopters close in around it.
Burns, hair loss and nausea reported.
Lawsuit dismissed: no evidence the craft belonged to the U.S. government.

records.title: Trans-en-Provence landing trace
records.place: Trans-en-Provence, Var
records.explanation: The French government’s GEPAN (now GEIPAN, part of CNES) analysed soil and plant samples and reported heating and biochemical changes it could not attribute to a known cause. Skeptics suggest a vehicle or the witness.
records.shape: Lead-grey disc, two stacked saucers
records.witnesses: Renato Nicolaï
records.summary: Renato Nicolaï heard a whistle and saw an object land briefly on his terrace and fly off. The Gendarmerie took samples within a day; GEPAN’s laboratory analysis of the 2.4 m circular mark reported soil heated to 300–600 °C and chlorophyll changes in alfalfa leaves.

timeline.text: Object lands and departs almost immediately.
Gendarmes photograph and sample the ring-shaped trace.
GEPAN Technical Note 16 published.

sources.label: GEIPAN — French government UAP case archive (CNES)

records.title: The spiral over south-west China
records.place: Sichuan and Yunnan, and across south-west, north-west and south-central China
records.explanation: Newspapers first quoted astronomers blaming a meteor shower; the astronomer Liu Yan of the Purple Mountain Observatory, who analysed the eyewitness reports, concluded it was a man-made object about 650 km up, and an article in the space magazine Hangtian put it at about 500 km and rejected the meteor idea. A slowly turning spiral of light seen from half a country is what a rocket stage venting propellant in sunlight looks like (compare the Norwegian and Australian spirals), but no launch has been matched to this one.
records.shape: A star-like point that brightened and grew a spinning, silver, spiral-shaped band of light
records.witnesses: Very many people across several provinces; the Hangtian article claims ten million
records.summary: At 10:38 p.m. on July 24, 1981, on a clear, moonless night, people across Sichuan, Yunnan, Gansu and neighbouring provinces saw a bright, star-like point grow brighter, begin to oscillate and develop a cloud-like band of light that turned into a huge silver spiral, spinning as it crossed the sky slowly from east to west. It was in view for six or seven minutes. The sighting started a nationwide craze for UFOs in the newly opened China; the U.S. Air Force’s Foreign Technology Division translated a Hangtian article about it, “UFO incident causes sensation throughout half of China”, which weighed a meteor, an aircraft and a flying saucer. Liu Yan, the Purple Mountain Observatory astronomer who handled many of the letters the public sent about UFOs in the 1980s, made it the subject of his first article on them and concluded it was man-made.

timeline.text: A star-like light brightens and grows a spiral band; seen across several provinces.
The spiral fades.
Newspapers quote astronomers suggesting a meteor shower.
Liu Yan concludes it was a man-made object about 650 km up.
The U.S. Air Force translates the Hangtian article on the sighting.

sources.label: “UFO incident causes sensation throughout half of China” (FTD translation, DTIC ADA133326)
The Black Vault — the translated Hangtian article
Sixth Tone — The astronomer who calmed China’s UFO craze

records.title: Hannah McRoberts’ photograph — Vancouver Island
records.place: A provincial park by the Eve River bridge on Highway 19, near Kelsey Bay, Vancouver Island, British Columbia
records.explanation: The NASA scientist Richard Haines examined the negative in 1987 and found no sign of tampering or a support thread; his measurements put the disc at least 30 feet from the camera, and interviews and a site survey supported the family’s account. Because nobody saw the object, a thrown object (a Frisbee, a hubcap or a pan lid have been suggested) cannot be ruled out, and later re-analyses from prints rather than the negative leave the case open.
records.shape: A sharply focused, domed disc against clear blue sky above a mountain peak
records.witnesses: None saw the object; the photographer, Hannah McRoberts, her husband and daughter were present
records.duration: One frame of 35 mm colour film
records.summary: At about 11 a.m. on October 8, 1981, Hannah McRoberts photographed a mountain peak from a provincial park off Highway 19 near Kelsey Bay, on the north-east coast of Vancouver Island, while travelling with her husband and young daughter. Nobody noticed anything in the sky. When the film was developed days later, one frame showed a sharply focused, dark, domed disc above the peak. Richard Haines, a perception scientist at NASA Ames, examined the original negative with micro-densitometry and computer enhancement, visited the site and interviewed the family; he found no evidence of a hoax, concluded the object was three-dimensional and at least 30 feet away, and presented the photograph to the 1997 Sturrock panel on UFO evidence. It is still one of the most reproduced UFO photographs, and one of the most argued over.

timeline.text: Hannah McRoberts photographs a peak from the park; nobody sees anything unusual.
The developed film shows a disc above the mountain.
Richard Haines analyses the negative and surveys the site.
The photograph is shown to the Sturrock panel.
Metabunk re-examines it and finds a thrown object possible.

sources.label: Patrick Gross — the McRoberts photograph and Haines’s analysis
Metabunk — Hannah McRoberts’ 1981 UFO revisited

records.title: Brest-Guipavas airport — the fireball by the runway
records.place: Brest-Guipavas airport, Finistère
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: GEIPAN class B: probably a meteoroid entering the atmosphere on a shallow path, seen nearly head-on, which explains the red-orange ball, the short, slow descent and the sudden disappearance. A radar “spot” first cited in the file was not supported: the controllers noted nothing abnormal.
records.shape: A red-orange ball, low on the horizon, that seemed to drop into a field by the runway
records.witnesses: Seven people in four independent groups: joggers, airport firefighters and a man waiting for a bus
records.duration: Seconds (15 s or less, by most accounts)
records.summary: At about 7:55 on the morning of November 22, 1981, in early light, people in four separate groups near Brest-Guipavas airport saw a red-orange ball low over the horizon that seemed to fall into a field beside a runway and vanish; some saw sparks or a short trail. The airport’s firefighters, who watched it come down as if landing, alerted the control tower. The gendarmes, contacted the next day by the air traffic controller, took eight statements and searched; no trace was found. GEPAN’s original file recorded a radar echo at the time, which made the case a class D, unexplained. GEIPAN’s re-examination found that the radar centre had treated the echoes as insignificant and that the controllers had seen nothing abnormal, and reclassified it B: a meteoroid on a grazing path, seen almost head-on.

timeline.text: A red-orange ball is seen low on the horizon by four groups of witnesses.
It seems to drop into a field by the runway and vanish; the firefighters alert the tower.
The gendarmes take statements; nothing is found on the ground.
GEPAN classes it D, citing a radar echo.
GEIPAN reclassifies it B: probably a meteoroid; the radar echo was not significant.

sources.label: GEIPAN case 1981-11-00900, Guipavas (in French)

records.title: Trancrainville — gendarmes on the A10 and the lit-up ground
records.place: A10 motorway near Trancrainville, Eure-et-Loir, north of Orléans
records.shape: An indistinct bright mass in the sky, and a strongly lit patch on the ground
records.witnesses: Two gendarmes of the motorway patrol
records.summary: Between 4:35 and 4:55 a.m. on January 23, 1982, two gendarmes of the motorway patrol, driving south on the A10, saw an indistinct bright mass in the sky and a strongly lit area on the ground beneath it, which moved across pylons and hangars. They followed it for about 30 km, driving and stopping, losing and finding it again, and heard nothing even with the engine off; at the end only a glow remained to the east over the trees. The Orléans air base, 7 km away, had nothing flying and its radar had been off since the evening before, and the motorway operator’s staff had seen nothing. Re-examining the case, GEIPAN rejected planets (they cannot light the ground) and judged a helicopter with a searchlight above the cloud, then at 1,200–1,500 m, too unlikely for the equipment of the time. It is class D, unexplained, with the caveat that no field interview could be made.

timeline.text: The patrol sees a bright mass in the sky and a lit patch on the ground.
They follow it about 30 km along the A10, losing and regaining it.
Only a glow remains to the east over the trees.
Checks: no flights from Orléans air base, radar off; motorway staff saw nothing.
GEIPAN: class D, a helicopter searchlight judged too unlikely.

sources.label: GEIPAN case 1982-01-00913, Trancrainville (in French)

records.title: VASP flight 169 — the light that paced a Boeing 727
records.place: Night flight from Fortaleza to Rio de Janeiro, first seen near Petrolina, Pernambuco
records.explanation: A study in the Journal of Scientific Exploration (2014) concluded the light was the planet Venus, rising brilliantly before dawn and possibly distorted by an atmospheric mirage. The captain rejected that, saying he knew Venus and the Moon; a radar return the air-traffic centre reported near the airliner has never been documented in detail.
records.shape: A bright light changing from red to orange, with a white and bluish centre
records.witnesses: Captain Gérson Maciel de Britto, his co-pilot and many passengers; crews of two other airliners
records.summary: VASP’s night flight 169, a Boeing 727 (PP-SNG) under Captain Gérson Maciel de Britto, left Fortaleza at 01:50 on February 8, 1982 for Rio de Janeiro. About half an hour later, near Petrolina, the captain saw a light approach on the left and pace the aircraft. It changed colour between red and orange around a white and bluish centre, seemed to move above and below the airliner, and stayed with it past Belo Horizonte; at 31,000 ft the crew said a bluish light filled the cabin. Britto called the air-traffic and air-defence centre CINDACTA in Brasília, which had no traffic there, dimmed his lights and flashed his landing lights at it, and woke the passengers; one compared it to a mercury street lamp. CINDACTA later said its radar showed a return about eight miles from the aircraft, and crews of a Transbrasil and an Aerolíneas Argentinas flight reported seeing something. The light was lost in cloud over the Serra do Mar a few minutes before landing at Galeão. The case was examined in the Journal of Scientific Exploration in 2014, which concluded that the “object” was Venus, very bright in the eastern pre-dawn sky.

timeline.text: Flight 169 leaves Fortaleza.
Near Petrolina the captain sees a light approach and pace the aircraft.
CINDACTA reports no traffic; the captain flashes his lights and wakes the passengers.
At 31,000 ft a bluish light seems to fill the cabin; CINDACTA reports a return about 8 miles away.
The light is lost in cloud over the Serra do Mar; the airliner lands at Galeão.
A journal study concludes the light was Venus, perhaps distorted by a mirage.

points.note: Lost in cloud over the Serra do Mar

records.title: Morenão stadium sighting
records.place: Estádio Morenão, Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul
records.shape: Unidentified lights
records.witnesses: More than 24,000 spectators, players and the referee
records.summary: During a Brazilian championship match between Operário and Vasco da Gama, a crowd of more than 24,000 saw unidentified objects over the stadium. Players, including Cocada, and referee José de Assis Aragão described them. Among the spectators was Ademar José Gevaerd, who went on to become one of Brazil's best-known UFO researchers.

records.title: Hessdalen lights
records.place: Hessdalen valley, Norway
records.explanation: Studied since 1983 by Project Hessdalen with an automated measurement station; hypotheses include combustion of dust from the valley’s ores, plasma, and piezoelectric effects.
records.shape: White, yellow or red floating lights
records.witnesses: Residents and scientists
records.summary: Lights have appeared over the 12-km Hessdalen valley since at least the early 1980s, peaking at up to 20 per week in 1981–84. Unusually, they have been measured: radar, spectra, magnetometers and a permanent camera station have recorded them, but their cause is still debated.

timeline.text: Peak activity; up to 20 sightings a week.
Project Hessdalen field campaign with radar and cameras.
Automated measurement station installed.

records.title: Hudson Valley "Westchester boomerang"
records.place: Brewster, Putnam County, New York
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: State police and the New York Power Authority attributed the sightings to pilots flying Cessna 152s in tight formation from Stormville Airport with coloured lights — a hoax the pilots reportedly enjoyed.
records.shape: V / boomerang of coloured lights
records.witnesses: Thousands across Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess and Fairfield counties
records.summary: For over a year residents of the Hudson Valley reported a silent boomerang or V of bright lights, sometimes "the size of a football field". Guards at the Indian Point nuclear plant reportedly saw it in June and July 1984, and a Brewster resident videotaped the lights on 24 July.

timeline.text: First wave of reports.
Claimed sightings over the Indian Point nuclear plant.
Bob Pozzuoli videotapes the lights in Brewster.

records.title: Aeroflot Tu-134 over Minsk — the light that became a cloud
records.place: Over Minsk, Byelorussian SSR, on the flight to Tallinn
records.explanation: Western analysts tied it to a Soviet missile launch that night, whose rising plume and glowing exhaust cloud look much like the crew’s sketches: Jonathan McDowell’s launch catalogue lists a submarine-launched R-29R test on September 7, 1984, with a note (after James Oberg) naming it as the source of the sighting. The Soviet army newspaper Krasnaya Zvezda suggested light refracted by floating space debris.
records.shape: A yellow light that threw out rays, became concentric circles and then a green cloud
records.witnesses: Captain Igor Cherkashin and co-pilot Gennady Lazurin of an Aeroflot Tu-134, and the crew of a second airliner
records.duration: Several minutes; the cloud is said to have stayed with the aircraft for hundreds of kilometres
records.summary: At about 4 a.m. on September 7, 1984, the crew of an Aeroflot Tu-134 flying from Tbilisi via Rostov to Tallinn saw a bright yellow light appear to their right over Byelorussia. It threw out beams strong enough, by one account, to light up the houses and roads below, changed into concentric circles and then into a glowing green cloud that seemed to follow the airliner. Co-pilot Gennady Lazurin sketched it, and Captain Igor Cherkashin called air traffic control, which reported a “double” return on radar; a second airliner flying the opposite way also saw it. The newspaper Trud published the story in early 1985, a rare UFO report in the Soviet press. Rumours that crew members of the second aircraft later died of illnesses caused by the encounter have never been substantiated. Western analysts matched the sketches to the plume of a missile launched that night.

timeline.text: A yellow light appears to the right of the Tu-134 near Minsk.
It turns into rays, circles and a green cloud; ground radar reports a double image.
Trud publishes the crew’s account.
Krasnaya Zvezda suggests light refracted by space debris.
Western analysts match the crew’s sketches to a missile launch that night.

sources.label: Le Figaro, 28 February 1985, reporting Trud (transcribed by Patrick Gross)

records.title: Dalnegorsk “Height 611” crash
records.place: Dalnegorsk, Primorsky Krai, Russia
records.explanation: Ball lightning and other plasma phenomena have been proposed. The reports of unusual metal fragments come mostly from the investigating group and have not been independently confirmed.
records.shape: Reddish sphere about 3 m across
records.witnesses: Residents of Dalnegorsk
records.summary: On the evening of January 29, 1986 residents of the mining town of Dalnegorsk saw a reddish, silent sphere about three metres across flying from the south-east at some 700–800 metres, at about 15 m/s. It crossed part of the town and came down on Izvestkovaya mountain, known as Height 611, burning on the slope. Investigators reported tiny metallic droplets 2–5 mm across, and fibres in a tangle of metal, quartz and gold-coloured threads. In Russia it is often called the best-documented UFO crash, although the technical findings come mainly from the group that investigated it.

timeline.text: A reddish sphere is seen crossing the town from the south-east.
It strikes Izvestkovaya mountain (Height 611) and burns.
A group led by Valeri Dvuzhilny collects droplets and fibres from the slope.

records.title: Brazil’s "Official UFO Night"
records.place: São José dos Campos – Rio de Janeiro – Goiás
records.explanation: The Air Force commander said "we have no explanation". The report declassified in 2009 described objects with speeds from hovering to supersonic and 90° turns.
records.shape: Red, white and green lights; 21 radar plots
records.witnesses: Controllers, F-5E and Mirage pilots, Embraer founder Ozires Silva
records.summary: Controllers at São José dos Campos and radar across south-east Brazil tracked about 21 unknown contacts. Embraer’s founder, flying in, saw red lights; the Air Force scrambled F-5Es from Santa Cruz and Mirage IIIs from Anápolis. Pilots reported lights that kept their distance and targets that appeared behind them.

records.title: Torpo film
records.place: Mountain farm near Torpo, Hallingdal
records.shape: Two bright objects, one flashing and throwing sparks
records.witnesses: A family and friends at a mountain farm
records.summary: A couple at a mountain farm near Torpo, with their son and friends, watched two bright objects in the evening sky, one moving dramatically, flashing and throwing off sparks. The husband filmed them. Ground Saucer Watch found no sign of a hoax, but said the apparent motion could come from camera shake and that the lack of reference points made the film inconclusive.

records.title: Japan Air Lines Flight 1628
records.place: Over north-east Alaska
records.explanation: The FAA’s radar returns were later dismissed as clutter / a split image; Philip Klass argued the crew saw Jupiter and Mars. The FAA found the crew professional and rational.
records.shape: Two small lights and a huge "mothership"
records.witnesses: Capt. Kenji Terauchi and crew
records.summary: A JAL Boeing 747 freighter on the Reykjavík–Anchorage leg reported three objects pacing it at 35,000 ft, including one Terauchi described as enormous. Anchorage controllers reported returns near the aircraft; the objects stayed with the plane through turns and descents until near Talkeetna.

timeline.text: Lights seen near the aircraft over eastern Alaska.
Crew reports to Anchorage ARTCC; traffic advisory.
Orbit and descent requested; lights stay with the jet.
Objects lost near Talkeetna; jet lands in Anchorage.

records.title: Gulf Breeze photographs
records.place: Gulf Breeze, Florida
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: Considered a hoax. In 1990 the new owners of Ed Walters's former house found a styrofoam model UFO in the attic that a reporter used to reproduce the photos almost exactly. A local teenager also said he had helped fake them. Walters said the model was planted.
records.shape: Cylindrical craft with a ring of portholes and a glowing base
records.witnesses: Ed Walters; other residents later came forward
records.summary: Contractor Ed Walters gave the Gulf Breeze Sentinel five Polaroids of a glowing craft he said hovered near his home. Over six months he produced dozens more photos and video, and described being hit by a blue beam and seeing aliens. Researchers such as Bruce Maccabee backed the photos, and other residents reported sightings. After the model was found in 1990 and a reporter recreated the pictures, the case became a textbook example of a UFO photo hoax.

timeline.text: Walters takes the first Polaroids outside his home.
Many more photos and video; other residents report lights.
Styrofoam model found in the attic of Walters's former house.

records.title: Ilkley Moor photograph
records.place: Ilkley Moor, West Yorkshire, England
records.explanation: Critics say the blurry photograph could show a person or a cardboard cutout, and ask why no picture of the craft was taken. Kodak experts found no sign of tampering, but the image is too grainy for firm conclusions, and the account changed under hypnosis.
records.shape: Small green humanoid; two-part silver craft
records.witnesses: Philip Spencer, a retired police officer (a pseudonym)
records.duration: Minutes; about two hours unaccounted for
records.summary: On the morning of December 1, 1987 Philip Spencer, a retired police officer, was walking across Ilkley Moor, between Ilkley and Keighley, when he said he met a small dark-green figure about 1.2 metres tall, with a large head and long thin arms. He took one photograph before it ran off, then saw a whitish, two-part craft rise from the moor with a loud hum. About two hours were missing from his journey, and his compass pointed the wrong way. A wildlife photographer said the figure matched no known animal and Kodak found no signs of tampering, but the US Navy optics specialist Bruce Maccabee called the image too grainy to test. Under hypnosis in March 1988 his story changed to one of being taken aboard and examined.

timeline.text: Spencer meets a small green figure on the moor and takes one photograph.
A whitish two-part craft rises from the moor with a loud humming sound.
He finds about two hours have passed, and that his compass points the wrong way.
Under regression hypnosis he recalls being taken aboard and examined.

records.title: Knowles family encounter
records.place: Nullarbor Plain, between Madura and Mundrabilla, Western Australia
records.explanation: No explanation has been established. The account rests on the four family members’ testimony and the physical details they described, and has been widely reported in Australia.
records.shape: Large glowing ball
records.witnesses: Faye Knowles and her sons Patrick, Sean and Wayne
records.summary: In the early hours of January 20, 1988, the Knowles family were driving across the Nullarbor Plain in their station wagon when a bright light appeared ahead. They said a large glowing object pursued the car for a long time and finally came down on the roof; the car seemed to be lifted off the road, and the engine and voices changed as if time were slowing. Mrs Knowles said she reached out of the rear window, felt something soft and warm on the roof, and found her hand covered in black dust. When the car dropped back onto the road a rear tyre burst. The family reported it at Mundrabilla. It is one of Australia’s best-known close-encounter stories.

timeline.text: A bright light is seen ahead; a glowing ball follows the car.
The object appears to settle on the roof and the car is lifted.
The car drops back onto the road and a rear tyre bursts; the family drives on and reports it at Mundrabilla.

sources.label: UFO Evidence — Knowles family encounter, Mundrabilla

records.place: Villa Urquiza, Buenos Aires
records.shape: Silver object
records.witnesses: More than 7,500
records.summary: On Christmas Day 1988 a silver object crossed the Villa Urquiza neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, watched by thousands of people. The city airport reported an object heading west toward Avenida General Paz. It is often called Argentina's most spectacular UFO sighting.

records.title: Kapustin Yar — the KGB file on a night of lights over a missile depot
records.place: Military sites 30–45 km from Kapustin Yar, Astrakhan oblast
records.explanation: The reports are in a package of 124 pages that the KGB sent to the cosmonaut Pavel Popovich in October 1991, with a covering letter saying that the KGB did not study UFO reports but passed on what it received. No investigation or conclusion accompanies them, and the original file was later said to have gone missing.
records.shape: A disc 4–5 m across with a dome, glowing dim green, with a bright flashing light and a beam
records.witnesses: Officers and soldiers of military units near Kapustin Yar, among them Ensign V. N. Voloshin, Capt. Chernikov and Sr Lt Klimenko
records.duration: About three and a half hours
records.summary: Between 22:10 on July 28 and 01:30 on July 29, 1989, soldiers and officers at military sites 30 to 45 km from the Kapustin Yar missile range, described in the reports as a transmission centre and a rocket-weapons depot, reported unidentified objects. At the depot, Ensign Valery Voloshin and a private watched through binoculars for about two hours as a disc some 4–5 m across with a dome, glowing a dim phosphorescent green, hovered 20 to 70 m above the warehouses, flashed a bright light and swept a beam, moved silently in sudden jerks, and finally left towards Akhtubinsk. Other officers described flashes like electric welding, a “flying plate” or a cigar-shaped object, and an aircraft was said to have been sent up but kept at a distance. The written statements, with unit names blacked out, were among 124 pages of military and civilian reports that the KGB passed in October 1991 to Pavel Popovich, president of a Soviet ufological association; Komsomolskaya Pravda published them in 2003. They are first-hand military reports, but nothing shows that anyone examined them.

timeline.text: Three objects are reported 3–5 km from a transmission centre.
At the depot, a glowing disc hovers over the warehouses and sweeps a beam.
An aircraft is reported sent up; the object keeps its distance.
The object leaves towards Akhtubinsk.
The KGB sends the reports to cosmonaut Pavel Popovich.
Komsomolskaya Pravda publishes the documents.

records.title: Voronezh park landing
records.place: Voronezh, RSFSR (Russia)
records.explanation: Reported by the Soviet news agency TASS; later widely regarded as a children’s story amplified by the press.
records.shape: Large red sphere / oval
records.witnesses: Mainly children in a city park
records.summary: TASS reported that children in a Voronezh park saw a large red ball land and tall beings emerge. Soviet reporting of the case — unusual at the time — made headlines worldwide.

timeline.text: Sighting in the park.
TASS publishes the account.

records.title: Pereslavl-Zalessky — the Soviet air defence report
records.place: Pereslavl-Zalessky region, north-east of Moscow
records.shape: A disc 100–200 m across with two pulsing lights on its sides
records.witnesses: More than 100 observers reported by air-defence units of the Moscow Military District; interceptor pilots Lt Col A. A. Semenchenko and others; radar crews
records.summary: On the night of March 21, 1990, air-defence units of the Moscow Military District reported more than 100 visual sightings of an object near Pereslavl-Zalessky. At 21:38 Lt Col A. A. Semenchenko was scrambled to identify a target at about 2,000 m; he saw two flashing white lights and a dim silhouette against the lights of the town, and the target did not answer his identification interrogation. Other pilots and radar posts gave times, bearings and distances; one ground radar post reported a fast-moving shining object with red lights, followed by another with white lights. In Rabochaya Tribuna on April 19, Colonel General Igor Maltsev, chief of the Main Staff of the Soviet Air Defence Forces, published excerpts: a disc 100 to 200 m across with two pulsing lights, flying silently between 1,000 and 7,000 m, at two to three times the speed of a modern fighter, rotating and hovering. Maltsev said he was “not a specialist on UFOs” and could only correlate the data. It was the first time a Soviet commander of that rank described such a case in public; the underlying reports have not been released, and no explanation was published.

timeline.text: Air-defence posts report a moving light; observations pass 100.

records.title: Crop circles — Doug Bower and Dave Chorley own up

They showed their tools, a plank, a rope and a cap with a wire loop to keep a straight line, and made a circle for journalists that the cerealogist Pat Delgado then declared authentic. Not every circle since is theirs, but none has been shown to have any cause other than people.

records.summary: On the night of March 8, 1994, dozens of people along the Lake Michigan shore of western Michigan called 911 about lights over the lake: five or six objects with red, green, blue and white lights that hovered and moved erratically. Over the following weeks more than 300 people in 42 Michigan counties reported sightings; MUFON investigators interviewed dozens and found no explanation. Bushong kept his account for decades, and the case stays one of the better-documented police and radar cases of the 1990s.

Jorge Polanco, was coming in to land at Bariloche when the airport lost power, and then the whole city went dark as the airliner neared the runway, forcing a go-around. A light “between white and amber”, like a star but much larger and brighter, then flew on a parallel course about 100 metres from the plane. The tower chief and the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne flying 600 metres higher saw it too, and the tower’s instruments swung from one direction to another for no clear reason. records.explanation: The British Geological Survey said the recorded signal was atmospheric, not an impact, and most likely a supersonic aircraft. The researcher David Clarke argues that a covert military flight continued after the exercise.

The Ministry of Defence first said no RAF aircraft was responsible, then admitted that six Tornados had been on low-flying training until 21:30, denied that any had gone supersonic, and closed the case after an RAF Police inquiry with “no military link”. records.place: Harbour Mille, Fortune Bay, Newfoundland
records.explanation: Canada and France both said no missile or rocket had been launched; France’s M51 test from the submarine Le Terrible was on a different day and did not match the time or direction. A Royal Military College engineer judged the object subsonic and much smaller than a missile; federal officials suggested model rockets, which the witnesses rejected; and a television station later aired viewer video from the same time that showed a passing aircraft, whose contrail lit by the setting sun would look like a fiery trail. records.witnesses: Spectators at an air show who filmed it; nobody saw the object at the time

An engineer from the nearby aircraft factory, reviewing his own video in slow motion, noticed a small object that seemed to loop near the jets, and handed it to CEFAA, the committee of the civil aviation directorate that studies aerial phenomena. CEFAA gathered seven videos from different spectators and, at a press conference on March 13, 2012, said an astronomer had ruled out a meteoroid, space debris, a bird and an aircraft, estimated the object’s speed at over 6,500 km/h and said the incident could not be explained scientifically. Nobody at the show had noticed anything. Critics pointed out that the speed holds only if the object was far away; analyses of the original frames by the HoaxKiller project and others found the shape and motion of an insect a few metres from the lens.

records.title: The “mystery missile” off Los Angeles — an airliner’s contrail
records.place: Over the Pacific about 35 miles west of Los Angeles, north of Santa Catalina Island
records.explanation: A condensation trail from an airliner flying towards the camera, which made a horizontal trail look like a vertical column lit by the setting sun. The FAA’s radar replays found no fast unidentified target, the Pentagon said there was no evidence it was anything else, and NASA’s contrail specialists found the trail on GOES-11 satellite imagery as a horizontal streak. US Airways Flight 808 from Honolulu and UPS Flight 902 were named as candidates.
records.shape: A thick, glowing vapour trail apparently rising from the sea, with a bright head
records.witnesses: A KCBS news-helicopter crew; many people in the Los Angeles area
records.summary: At about 5:15 p.m. on November 8, 2010, a KCBS news helicopter filmed what looked like a missile climbing from the sea about 35 miles west of Los Angeles, a thick vapour trail glowing orange against the sunset with a bright point at its head. The footage ran on every network as the “mystery missile”, and for a day and a half nobody official could say what it was: the Pentagon said it was not a Defense Department launch, NORAD and Northern Command said it was no foreign military launch and no threat, the Navy said it was not theirs, and the FAA had approved no commercial launch. Contrail specialists and the analyst John Pike said at once that it was an aircraft contrail seen end-on, the head of the trail moving far too slowly for a rocket; the FAA’s radar replays found no fast unknown target, and on November 10 the Pentagon said there was “no evidence to suggest that this is anything else other than a condensation trail from an aircraft.” NASA researchers later found the trail on the GOES-11 weather-satellite image as a long horizontal streak. A few experts said they could not rule out a missile, but the incident is now a textbook example of foreshortened perspective.

records.title: The light over the Dome of the Rock (hoax)
records.place: Dome of the Rock, Temple Mount (Haram al-Sharif), Old City of Jerusalem
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: The videos were faked. They were posted anonymously; nobody else among the many people in and around the Old City reported the light; it casts no reflection on the gilded dome; one clip was filmed off a monitor screen; and the analyst Robert Sheaffer showed that the camera shake had been added with an edge-mirroring “motion tile” effect. Nobody has owned up, but no one who examined the clips found them genuine.

records.witnesses: The anonymous uploaders of four videos; no independent witness
records.summary: In late January 2011 a YouTube video appeared showing a small bright light dropping slowly toward the Dome of the Rock some time after midnight on January 28, hovering just above the golden dome, flashing, and then shooting straight up out of sight. A second clip from another angle followed, then two more, posted under the challenge “Have fun debunking this one”. The videos went round the world, with commentators noting that the multiple viewpoints made them hard to dismiss. Within days investigators pointed to the anonymous sources, the lack of any other witness in one of the most watched places on Earth, the missing reflection on the dome and signs of editing, and the case became a standard example of a digitally inserted UFO.

records.witnesses: Indian Army and Indo-Tibetan Border Police troops

records.summary: From August 2012, soldiers and border police on the Line of Actual Control in eastern Ladakh reported luminous objects rising over the Chinese side and staying up for hours. With Chinese drones a real concern, the army logged 329 sightings by February 2013 and counted 155 apparent violations of the border. At the army’s request, two astronomers from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics in Bengaluru travelled to Thakung, near Pangong Tso, and measured the objects with a theodolite: one was visible from about 6 p.m. to 5 a.m., the other from about 4 a.m., and they moved with the stars. They were Jupiter and Venus. A soldier’s note that one object rose about four minutes earlier every day, as a planet does, had already pointed the same way.

records.title: Chelyabinsk meteor — and the “UFO that shot it down”
records.place: Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia; the air burst south of Chelyabinsk
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: A near-Earth asteroid about 20 m across entered at about 19 km/s at a shallow angle and exploded some 30 km up with the energy of roughly 400–500 kilotons of TNT, recorded by infrasound stations worldwide and by U.S. government sensors. Meteorites were collected across the strewn field, and a 654 kg fragment was raised from Lake Chebarkul in October 2013. Claims that videos showed a UFO destroying the meteor, and a newspaper survey in which many readers preferred a weapon test or a crashing alien ship, rest on nothing but the footage of the meteor itself.
records.shape: A fireball brighter than the Sun, leaving a long, twisted smoke trail
records.witnesses: Hundreds of thousands in Chelyabinsk Oblast and neighbouring regions; filmed by hundreds of dashboard and security cameras
records.duration: About 15 seconds of flight; the shock wave arrived one to three minutes later
records.summary: At 9:20 a.m. on February 15, 2013, a fireball brighter than the Sun crossed the morning sky of the southern Urals from the east and exploded south of Chelyabinsk, leaving a smoke trail tens of kilometres long. A minute or more later the shock wave blew in windows across the city: 1,491 people sought medical help, most cut by glass, and more than 7,000 buildings were damaged. Because Russian drivers routinely run dashboard cameras, the event was filmed from hundreds of angles, which let scientists reconstruct its path and orbit within days. Within hours, too, clips circulated claiming that a small object had flown into the meteor and shattered it, and the UFO commentator Gennady Belimov said a UFO had shot it down; a survey by the newspaper Noviye Izvestia found barely half its readers accepted the official account. The fragments in museum collections are ordinary chondrite.

A CEFAA analyst at the meteorological office ruled out lenticular cloud, aircraft, drones, balloons and birds, found the object brighter than reflected sunlight would make it, and concluded it “can be qualified as a UFO”; the director, retired General Ricardo Bermúdez, released the study in July 2014 but said it was one analyst’s view and that the committee had to be cautious. The witnesses never answered CEFAA’s requests to talk, the originals and the order of the pictures were uncertain, and critics noted that a disc against blue sky gives no way to judge its size or distance. CEFAA filed the case as unexplained.

records.title: Naga fireballs of the Mekong
records.place: The Mekong around Phon Phisai and Nong Khai, Thailand, and the Lao bank opposite

records.shape: Reddish-pink balls of light rising silently from the river to a few hundred metres
records.witnesses: Tens of thousands of festival visitors each year
records.duration: Seconds each; tens to thousands a night, on the night of Ok Phansa
records.summary: Every year on the night of Wan Ok Phansa, the full moon that ends the Buddhist Rains Retreat in October, crowds gather along a 250 km stretch of the Mekong centred on Phon Phisai to watch glowing reddish balls rise silently from the water, climb a few hundred metres and vanish. Local belief credits the phaya nak, the serpent said to live in the river; until the mid-1980s they were called ghost lights, and the Phayanak festival now draws tens of thousands of visitors. The photograph here was taken near Nong Khai on Ok Phansa night, 2013. Sceptics point to gunfire and flares from the Lao bank, which the crowds would not hear across the river; believers point out that the lights also appear over ponds and smaller rivers away from the border.

timeline.text: The lights are known locally as ghost lights.

records.title: Chilean Navy helicopter FLIR video
records.place: Coast between San Antonio and Quinteros, Chile
records.explanation: Chile’s aerial-phenomena office (CEFAA) left the case open because it could not be certain of the object’s nature. Later analyses by sceptics proposed an aircraft’s contrail and exhaust seen by infrared as the likely cause.

records.witnesses: Navy helicopter crew (pilot and camera operator)
records.summary: On November 11, 2014 a Chilean Navy helicopter on coastal patrol west of Santiago, at about 4,500 feet, picked up an unknown object on its high-definition infrared camera. The two-man crew also saw it with the naked eye for more than ten minutes. The captain described a flat, elongated object with two thermal discharges that did not line up with its direction of travel, and the video shows what looks like a chemical plume. The Navy’s aerial-phenomena office CEFAA examined it and later released the footage, saying it could not be sure what it was. Sceptics later said the images match the contrail of a distant aircraft.

records.title: The light over California — a Trident II test from USS Kentucky
records.place: The Navy’s Pacific Test Range off Southern California; seen from California, Nevada and Arizona
records.explanation: An unarmed Trident II (D5) ballistic missile fired by the submarine USS Kentucky during a scheduled test in the Pacific Test Range. The Navy confirmed it the same evening; its exhaust plume, lit by sunlight high above the darkened ground, produced the expanding “twilight phenomenon”.
records.shape: A bright light trailing a glowing, expanding cone of blue-white vapour
records.witnesses: Thousands of people from San Francisco to San Diego, Las Vegas and Phoenix
records.summary: Shortly after 6 p.m. on Saturday, November 7, 2015, a bright light rose over the Pacific west of Los Angeles and grew into a glowing, spreading cone of vapour that was seen from the Bay Area to San Diego and as far as Nevada and Arizona. Police and sheriff’s offices across Southern California were flooded with calls, and the videos spread across social media as a UFO, a meteor or a missile gone wrong. The Navy said that evening that its Strategic Systems Programs had carried out a scheduled test flight of an unarmed Trident II D5 missile from USS Kentucky in the Pacific Test Range; such launches are not announced in advance. The effect, sunlight catching the exhaust plume high above a darkened ground, is the same as the Iridium launch of 2017 and many Vandenberg twilight launches before it.

records.title: Fireball over the West — a Chinese rocket stage re-entering
records.place: Across California, Nevada and Utah
records.explanation: The Joint Space Operations Center confirmed that the objects were the second stage of China’s Long March 7 rocket, launched on its first flight on June 25, 2016, re-entering the atmosphere and breaking up.
records.shape: A slow procession of bright fragments with glowing trails
records.witnesses: Thousands of people in California, Nevada, Utah, Idaho and Colorado
records.duration: More than 30 seconds in view from most places
records.summary: At about 9:36 p.m. on July 27, 2016, a slow procession of bright fragments with long trails crossed the sky over California, Nevada and Utah, seen from Los Angeles to Las Vegas and Salt Lake City and filmed by many people. It moved far more slowly than a meteor. Within hours the Joint Space Operations Center at Vandenberg confirmed that it had tracked the re-entry of the spent second stage of China’s new Long March 7 rocket, launched a month earlier, and later removed the object from the satellite catalogue as decayed. The astronomer Jonathan McDowell identified the stage from the tracking data. Like the Zond IV fragments of 1968, it is the kind of event that turns into a “formation of craft” in some witnesses’ descriptions.

records.title: Jeffreys Bay — a cargo crew’s green light
records.place: About 10 nautical miles off Jeffreys Bay, Eastern Cape
records.explanation: A green parachute flare was suspected first and ruled out because a flare cannot climb that high; the NSRI found no vessel or aircraft overdue or missing. Port Elizabeth air traffic control, fearing a vessel or aircraft in distress had fired a flare, asked the National Sea Rescue Institute to check; its Jeffreys Bay station watched overnight. The object was not seen again and no craft was overdue.

records.title: AARO’s “Southeast Asia Triangles” — fishing nets
records.place: A river in Southeast Asia (exact location withheld)
records.explanation: AARO, with intelligence and three science-and-technology partners, found “almost certainly” static, cone-shaped fishing nets on a river, each about 11 by 7 m, matched in other satellite images from 2017, 2022 and 2023 and in stock footage of the same river.
records.shape: Six dark triangles in a line
records.witnesses: An intelligence analyst reviewing satellite imagery
records.summary: A commercial satellite image taken at 07:35 UTC on August 30, 2017 showed six dark triangles in a staggered line, and an intelligence analyst flagged them as possibly anomalous and a risk to navigation. AARO reviewed the case in 2023. Its partners found a clearer image of the same place from February 2017 that showed the triangles as cone-shaped fishing nets anchored in a river, all about 11 by 7 metres; later images from late 2022 and early 2023 showed the same shapes with turbidity trailing downstream, proving they were in the water, and stock footage showed such nets on that river. AARO closed the case as fishing nets. Its report names only “Southeast Asia”; the image’s time stamps, 07:35Z and 14:05 local, match Myanmar’s clock (UTC+6:30), and the marker is placed there only approximately.

records.title: The Los Angeles “UFO” — SpaceX Iridium-4 launch
records.place: Vandenberg Air Force Base; seen across Southern California and as far as Arizona
records.explanation: A scheduled Falcon 9 launch carrying ten Iridium NEXT satellites from Vandenberg; the exhaust plume, lit by the Sun after sunset on the ground, made the glowing cloud. The Los Angeles Fire Department issued an advisory that the light came from the launch.
records.shape: A glowing, expanding jellyfish-like cloud with a bright point at its head
records.witnesses: Thousands across Southern California, Nevada and Arizona
records.summary: At 5:27 p.m. on December 22, 2017, twenty minutes after sunset, a Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg carrying ten Iridium NEXT satellites. High above the darkening ground the exhaust was still in sunlight, and the expanding plume, the staging and the fairing separation drew a luminous, jellyfish-like cloud seen from Los Angeles to Las Vegas and Phoenix. Phones and social media filled with pictures of a UFO; the Los Angeles Fire Department put out an advisory that the “mysterious light in the sky” was the launch, and Elon Musk posted the video as a “nuclear alien UFO from North Korea”. The launch had been announced in advance; twilight launches from Vandenberg have caused the same reports since.

timeline.text: The Falcon 9 lifts off from SLC-4E with ten Iridium NEXT satellites.

records.place: Over southern Arizona, east of the Sonoran Desert National Monument
records.explanation: An FAA spokesperson suggested a high-altitude balloon, which need not carry a transponder or tell air traffic control; the area sees regular research and weather balloons. The controller could not see anything on radar, and the pilots, who saw it pass above and in the opposite direction, did not sound convinced. No report of a military aircraft or drone in the area emerged.
records.shape: A bright, reflective object several thousand feet above the airliners
records.witnesses: The crew of a Phoenix Air Learjet 36 and of American Airlines Flight 1095, an Airbus A321; the Albuquerque Center controller
records.duration: About six minutes for both reports
records.summary: On the afternoon of February 24, 2018, a Learjet 36 flying east at about 37,000 ft over southern Arizona asked Albuquerque Center whether anything had just passed over it; the controller had nothing, and the pilot said something had. The controller asked American Airlines Flight 1095, an Airbus A321 following on the same route, to watch for traffic above it within the next 15 miles; a few minutes later its crew reported that something had passed over them, two or three thousand feet higher, going the other way, and, asked whether it was moving or hovering, said it was very bright or reflective. Someone on the frequency suggested a Google balloon, which the airline crew doubted, and someone else called it a UFO. The FAA released the recording to reporters in March; it said the controller could not see any other aircraft and suggested a high-altitude balloon. Nothing more was published.

records.place: Atlantic off County Kerry, Ireland
records.explanation: One pilot suggested a meteor or an object in re-entry, and an astronomer at the Armagh Observatory said the lights were most likely meteors. Air traffic control saw nothing on radar and no military exercises were running, so nothing has been confirmed.

records.witnesses: Crews of a British Airways and a Virgin Atlantic flight, and others
records.summary: At about 6:47 on the morning of November 9, 2018 the pilot of a British Airways flight from Montreal to London radioed Shannon air traffic control to ask whether military exercises were under way. A “very bright light” had come up on the left of the aircraft and “rapidly veered to the north”, then disappeared at very high speed. The crew of a Virgin Atlantic flight reported two bright lights that banked to the right and climbed away at what the pilot called “astronomical” speed, “like Mach 2”. Controllers saw nothing on radar, and no military exercises were taking place. The Irish Aviation Authority said it would investigate by confidentially interviewing the pilots. More than one crew reported it, and the story was carried by news outlets around the world.

records.explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the leaked clips were taken by Navy personnel. Analysts attribute the "pyramids" to the triangular aperture of a night-vision lens (bokeh) on aircraft/stars, and the Omaha sphere to a distant aircraft or balloon.

records.title: Colorado and Nebraska drone swarms
records.place: Phillips County and the plains of north-eastern Colorado
records.explanation: State and federal agencies found that most reports were planets, stars, aircraft and hobby drones, and the Colorado Department of Public Safety stood its effort down in January 2020. The large, grid-flying drones of the first reports were never tied to an operator.
records.shape: Drones with a wingspan of about 6 ft and blinking lights, in groups of six to ten, flying grid patterns
records.witnesses: Ranchers, residents and county sheriff’s deputies
records.summary: In December 2019, residents and deputies in north-eastern Colorado and western Nebraska began reporting drones with wingspans of about six feet flying in groups of six to ten, at 200 to 500 feet, in grid patterns across the plains, mostly between about 7 and 10 p.m.; one witness counted 19. County sheriffs asked the public for information, and more than 70 local, state and federal agencies met in Brush on January 6, 2020. The FAA said no drone company or test site had authorized flights there, and the Air Force, which had run counter-drone exercises at F. E. Warren AFB, would neither claim nor deny the drones. As the sightings spread, more and more turned out to be planets, stars and airliners, and the state ended its search later that month.

records.title: Sendai’s white balloon
records.place: Over Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan
records.explanation: A balloon. On February 14, 2023, after the Chinese balloon was shot down over the United States, Japan’s Ministry of Defense said that the balloons seen over its territory in November 2019, June 2020 and September 2021 were “strongly presumed” to be unmanned reconnaissance balloons flown by China; China rejected the claim.
records.shape: A large white sphere with crossed struts and propellers hanging beneath
records.witnesses: Residents of Sendai and Miyagi; the Sendai City Observatory photographed it
records.summary: On the morning of June 17, 2020, residents of northern Sendai began posting photographs of a large white sphere hanging almost motionless in the sky, with crossed struts and propellers beneath it. The Sendai office of the Japan Meteorological Agency said it looked like a weather balloon “but it’s not ours”, police sent a helicopter but could not identify it, Kyushu University denied it was theirs, and the government said only that it was aware of the object, which later drifted out over the Pacific. In February 2023, after the Chinese balloon crossed the United States, Japan’s Ministry of Defense re-examined the Sendai balloon and similar ones over Kagoshima in 2019 and Aomori in 2021, and concluded that they were strongly presumed to be Chinese unmanned reconnaissance balloons. It protested to Beijing, which said Japan had no proof.

timeline.text: A white balloon with a frame and propellers is seen hovering over Sendai.
The weather agency says it is not theirs; the government says it is aware of it.
The balloon drifts east over the Pacific and is lost.

records.place: Northeastern New Mexico, at about 36,000 ft

American Airlines at first denied that it was authentic, then confirmed that it was from Flight 2292 after talking to the crew. The FAA said controllers saw nothing on radar, and the Pentagon said it had no tests in the area.

records.title: Lights over Seattle and Portland — a Falcon 9 stage re-entering
records.place: Over western Oregon and Washington; debris in Grant County, Washington
records.explanation: The second stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 that launched Starlink satellites on March 4, 2021, failed to make its de-orbit burn and re-entered uncontrolled about three weeks later. The National Weather Service in Seattle identified the lights the same night, and a pressure vessel from the stage was found on a farm in Grant County, Washington, and recovered by SpaceX.
records.shape: A cluster of bright fragments with glowing trails, moving slowly across the sky
records.witnesses: Thousands of people in western Oregon and Washington
records.summary: At about 9 p.m. on March 25, 2021, people from Portland to Seattle saw a slow cluster of bright lights with trails cross the sky, breaking apart as it went, and posted videos of what many took for a meteor shower or a formation of craft. The National Weather Service office in Seattle said that night that the lights were the remnants of a Falcon 9 second stage re-entering; the astronomer Jonathan McDowell confirmed that the stage, left in orbit after a Starlink launch on March 4 when its de-orbit burn failed, had come down at about 04:00 UTC on March 26. Days later a farmer in Grant County, in central Washington, reported to the sheriff an object that had left a four-inch dent in his field: a composite-overwrapped pressure vessel from the stage, which SpaceX identified and collected. It is one of the few re-entries where the identification, the tracking and a piece of the object all came together.

timeline.text: A Falcon 9 launches Starlink satellites; its second stage fails to de-orbit.
The stage re-enters over the Pacific Northwest; bright fragments are seen and filmed.

A pressure vessel from the stage is found on a Grant County farm and recovered by SpaceX.

records.title: The blue spiral over New Zealand — a Falcon 9 upper stage
records.place: Across New Zealand, photographed from Queenstown, Stewart Island and Motueka
records.explanation: The upper stage of the SpaceX Falcon 9 that launched the Globalstar FM15 satellite from Cape Canaveral at 04:27 UTC that day, venting its leftover propellant before the burn that brought it down into the Pacific. records.summary: From mid-November 2024, residents in Morris County reported large, lighted drones flying at night, including over Picatinny Arsenal and near the president-elect's golf club in Bedminster. Reports spread across New Jersey and into New York, Pennsylvania and beyond. The FAA placed temporary flight restrictions over dozens of sites. Stewart International Airport briefly closed its runways, and many viral videos turned out to show airliners.

timeline.text: First wave of reports in Morris County.
FAA flight restrictions over Picatinny Arsenal and Bedminster.
Stewart International Airport closes runways for about an hour.
Federal joint statements: no national-security threat found.
White House: the drones were authorized by the FAA.

records.title: Drones over the U.S. air bases in England
records.place: RAF Lakenheath, Mildenhall, Feltwell and Fairford, England
records.explanation: The U.S. Air Force and the Ministry of Defence confirmed the drones, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an investigation, but the operators were not identified.
records.shape: Small drones of varying number and type
records.witnesses: U.S. Air Force personnel; residents of nearby villages
records.summary: Between November 20 and 26, 2024, small drones were seen over and around four bases in England used by the U.S. Air Force: RAF Lakenheath, home of the 48th Fighter Wing, RAF Mildenhall, RAF Feltwell and RAF Fairford. The Air Force said “small unmanned aerial systems were spotted in the vicinity of and over RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall and RAF Feltwell between 20 and 22 November”. Air traffic into Mildenhall was disrupted: on November 21 a KC-46 tanker that had brought F-35s across the Atlantic turned back and diverted to Prestwick. British troops with counter-drone equipment were sent to help, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an inquiry. Similar reports came from U.S. bases in Germany that December.

timeline.text: Drones are reported over and near Lakenheath, Mildenhall and Feltwell.
A KC-46 tanker bound for Mildenhall diverts to Prestwick because of drone reports.
More incursions, including at Fairford; British counter-drone teams are deployed.
The Ministry of Defence Police open an investigation; the operators remain unknown.

records.title: The drones that closed Europe’s airports
records.place: Copenhagen Airport first; then Oslo, Aalborg, Billund, Munich, Brussels and Liège
records.explanation: No one has been identified. Danish leaders at first spoke of a “capable actor” and Russia was widely suspected, but in June 2026 Copenhagen police said they had been unable to prove or rule out that drones were over the airport at all on September 22, and that they “were not clear enough” with their reservations.
records.shape: Two or three large drones with lights, seen repeatedly in the airport’s airspace
records.witnesses: Copenhagen police and airport staff; police, air traffic control and the public at the later airports
records.duration: Copenhagen closed for nearly four hours; the closures ran from September to November
records.summary: On the evening of September 22, 2025, Copenhagen Airport stopped all flights for nearly four hours after two or three large drones were reported again and again in its controlled airspace; police chose not to shoot them down over a populated area. Oslo Gardermoen closed briefly the same night. Over the next days Aalborg was shut twice, Billund for an hour and reports came from Esbjerg, Sønderborg and the Skrydstrup air base. On October 2 and 3 Munich stopped flights for hours, stranding thousands, and in November Brussels and Liège closed briefly. It is the European counterpart of the New Jersey drones of 2024: an airport closed is a fact, but what was in the air is still not established.

timeline.text: Copenhagen Airport closes for nearly four hours; Oslo closes briefly.
Aalborg closes twice; Billund for about an hour.
Munich suspends flights on two evenings.
Brussels Airport closes temporarily.
Liège Airport closes for just under an hour.
Copenhagen police say they can neither prove nor rule out drones on Sep 22.

records.title: Campo Largo — an influencer’s lights traced to a campsite
records.place: Rural Campo Largo, Paraná
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: An image analyst who worked from the filming position showed the lights came from an escarpment by a campsite, Chácara Paraíso, about 10 km away, distorted by distance and the air; the campsite’s lights are off when it is empty, which is why they were not seen every night. The Brazilian Air Force said its air-defence radars detected nothing unusual.
records.shape: A ring of lights alternating in brightness above the trees
records.witnesses: The influencer Mayk Leão, alone on his farm
records.summary: On May 31, 2026, Mayk Leão, a nursing technician and social-media influencer who lives alone on a remote farm in Campo Largo, Paraná, said his animals had been agitated, an electric fence was knocked down and he had heard metallic clicks, roars and mechanical noises; that evening he filmed bright lights in a circular group over a forested valley several kilometres away for twenty to forty minutes, and later drew a second, larger object he said passed over the property. His live streams and videos reached millions within days and drew national coverage. The Brazilian Air Force’s airspace department said its radars detected no unknown object, and internet users compared the sounds with a film trailer. Working from the coordinates of the farm, an image analyst then showed that the lights matched an escarpment beside a campsite, Chácara Paraíso, about 10 km away, whose lights are switched off when it has no guests.

timeline.text: Leão reports noises and a broken fence, then films lights over the forest.
The videos go viral; the Air Force says its radars detected nothing unknown.
An analysis traces the lights to the Chácara Paraíso campsite about 10 km away.
